newsitem.title: GERMANY: No reason to expect EMU delay - Bundesbank's Issing.
newsitem.headline: No reason to expect EMU delay - Bundesbank's Issing.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday there was no reason to expect European monetary union (EMU) would be delayed from its January 1999 start date.
But Issing said German May unemployment data would create additional problems for Bonn's budget, and its attempts to meet deficit criteria for entry into the planned single European currency.
"So far there is no reason to expect or suspect that EMU will not start on time," Issing told reporters at a Bundesbank conference.
Issing said technical preparations for monetary union had to be maintained.
He also said it was obvious that Germany was "not on a good way" to solving its jobless problems.
Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said on Friday he could no longer endorse the government's official forecast of 3.95 million average unemployment in 1997.
German unemployment rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.358 million in May, the labour office said on Friday.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, fell to 11.1 percent from 11.3 percent in April.
Issing said the May report was "bad for anyone in Germany".
"This increases the problems of tax receipts for the Finance Minister," Issing said of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's attempts to cut Germany's budget deficit.
